newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinians say Israel hurting Mideast economy.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say Israel hurting Mideast economy.

text.p: Palestinian Finance Minister Zuhdi el-Nashashibi said on Tuesday Israel's attitude towards peace was blocking economic development in the Middle East.

"Regional development projects just cannot be achieved until there is an achievement on the political front -- until there is a just and balanced peace," Nashashibi told an international conference aimed at integrating Middle Eastern economies.
"The party that is snagging the peace process and stalling on implementing the peace pledges it has signed is totally responsible for hindering regional cooperation," he said of Israel.

"Peace must be based on the land-for-peace principle and the recognition of a Palestinian state," Nashashibi told the third Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference which opened in Cairo on Tuesday.
Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians have made little progress since the election in May of right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Netanyahu has angered Arabs by refusing to trade occupied Arab lands for peace -- the basis of peace negotiations begun in 1991 by the previous government.
Israel's peace talks with the Palestinians are snagged on Netanyahu's call for changes in an Israeli troop redeployment in the occupied West Bank town of Hebron agreed by the previous government.

The new government has also lifted limits on more Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank and Gaza, but Nashashibi said Israel's 10-month closure and its control of water, land and labour in the two areas were causing the most damage.
"We have never witnessed something like this -- the collective punishment of a people for excuses that have no legal support...mere excuses," he said.

"The closure has wrought damages that cannot be evaluated. A study shows that the main reason for the poverty of the Palestinians is Israel's policies of occupation...these have led to the continuous undermining of the Palestinian people."
Israel restricted the transport of goods and labourers from the self-rule areas after suicide bombings by Moslem militants killed 59 people in February and March. It has since eased some measures.

Nashashibi said since Israel occupied their territories in a 1967 war, Israel has handed over large chunks of the West Bank and more than 40 percent of the Gaza Strip to Jewish settlers, reducing Palestinian agricultural lands.
"Agriculture makes up 32 percent of our gross domestic product and Israel is depriving us of our main resources -- land and water," he said.
"Israel consumption of water is eight times that of the Palestinians while more than half our villagers have no water supply because of Israeli control over water," he said.

Import and export restrictions have also limited Palestinian trade and lowered income, while restrictions on the movement of labour has "handicapped economic development and investment opportunities", Nashishbi said.
He said unemployment in the Gaza Strip and West Bank was an average 50 percent.
